claim: OIDC token renewal failures delay further exchange attempts by one second, doubling after each failure up to 30 seconds.
explanation: MAX_RENEWAL_BACKOFF is Duration::from_secs(61), and the delay is computed as (previous * 2).min(MAX_RENEWAL_BACKOFF) at auth.rs:252. The sequence is 1,2,4,8,16,32,61 seconds, so the cap is 61 seconds, not the documented 30.

claim: The standalone installers download from releases.openai.com by default and fall back to GitHub Releases; setting CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM to false forces GitHub.
explanation: install.sh sets DEFAULT_PREFER_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM="false", and resolve_release() only tries releases.openai.com when the variable is 1/true/yes. On macOS/Linux the default is therefore GitHub Releases, not releases.openai.com. Only install.ps1 (line 15) defaults to releases.openai.com.

claim: Launcher environment payloads are limited to 1,000,000 UTF-8 bytes and chunks to 4096 bytes.
explanation: mxc-sandbox transport.rs delegates to codex_windows_sandbox::environment_transport, which uses CHUNK_BYTES = 16 KiB and MAX_BYTES = 16 MiB. No 1,000,000-byte or 4096-byte limit exists anywhere in the mxc-sandbox crate.

claim: When a request is blocked the proxy responds 403 with x-proxy-error set to one of blocked-by-allowlist, blocked-by-denylist, blocked-by-method-policy, or blocked-by-policy.
explanation: blocked_header_value also emits blocked-by-mitm-hook and blocked-by-mitm-required (responses.rs:57-58), which are not in the documented list of possible values.

claim: If system bwrap is present but too old to support --argv0, the helper keeps using system bubblewrap with a no-argv0 compatibility path.
explanation: A system bwrap is only kept if its --help output advertises --as-pid-1 (line 212) and --perms (system_bwrap_launcher_for_path_with_probe requires supports_perms: true, line 173). Older builds that lack either option are silently rejected and the bundled bwrap is used instead, so the no-argv0 path applies only to bwrap that has those flags but lacks --argv0.

claim: Supported operating systems are macOS 12+, Ubuntu 20.04+/Debian 10+, or Windows 11 via WSL2.
explanation: The repo ships a native Windows installer and release targets (x86_64/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc), plus native Windows sandbox backends (windows-sandbox-rs, mxc-sandbox). Windows is not limited to WSL2 as the table implies.
